prompt:
You watch a short video made ONLY of these clips, played back to back with NO narration between them.
Each clip is a person's own words from a show; the shows were not in one conversation. The first clip (label "hook")
opens the video.

CLIP label="hook" (on screen: The Bitcoin Layer): "Bitcoin started turning though before liquidity turned red. And that's an important caveat here."
CLIP label="clip_01" (on screen: DataDash): "The Bitcoin capital markets are still in their early stages. But the opportunity to put Bitcoin to work through staking, collateral, and decentralized financial applications is still worth paying attention to."
CLIP label="clip_02" (on screen: CNBC Television): "I don't really think Bitcoin and crypto are partisan issues, right? Bitcoin and crypto are about how do we modernize the financial markets and how we would create financial freedom for 350 Americans and 8 billion people around the world."
CLIP label="clip_03" (on screen: What Bitcoin Did): "I will bet you one Bitcoin that RSA has broken in 10 years, and I'll bet you half a Bitcoin that it's broken in five years. That's the level of conviction I have."
CLIP label="clip_04" (on screen: Altcoin Daily): "I think treasury companies will also bleed to Bitcoin. I mean, basically, everything in the industry eventually bleeds to Bitcoin."

1) Played back to back with no narration, is there a through-line a viewer can state? State it in ONE sentence, or
   "none" if there is none.
2) THE HOOK is judged on its own job, NOT on the through-line. Rate each of its three parts 1-5 separately:
   "scroll": do its first 2-3 seconds stop a viewer from scrolling past? (5 = certainly, 1 = not at all)
   "alone": does it stand alone, so that a viewer needs nothing said before it? (5 = fully, 1 = not at all)
   "setup": does it set up what follows, so that a viewer who hears it wants the next clip? (5 = certainly, 1 = not
   at all)
3) For each clip AFTER the hook, rate 1-5 how much it advances that through-line (5 = essential, 1 = off topic).
4) For each JOIN between two consecutive clips: could a viewer follow the jump with no narration, i.e. is the next
   clip's subject or referent clear coming from the previous clip's ending? Answer true or false, and why in a few
   words.
Return ONLY this JSON object: {"through_line": "...", "hook": {"scroll": 1, "alone": 1, "setup": 1},
"clips": {"clip_01": 1, "clip_02": 1, "clip_03": 1, "clip_04": 1}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_02 -> clip_03": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_03 -> clip_04": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}}}
text: {"through_line": "Bitcoin is quietly becoming the center of a new financial system — its markets, its promise of financial freedom, its technology, and its gravitational pull on the whole industry.", "hook": {"scroll": 2, "alone": 2, "setup": 2}, "clips": {"clip_01": 4, "clip_02": 4, "clip_03": 2, "clip_04": 5}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "Both are about Bitcoin; 'capital markets' loosely continues the liquidity/markets thread, though the hook's caveat is never resolved."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "New speaker, but 'Bitcoin and crypto' names the subject, so it reads as another voice on the same theme."}, "clip_02 -> clip_03": {"followable": false, "why": "RSA drops in with no setup; only the 'one Bitcoin' stake ties it back to the previous clip."}, "clip_03 -> clip_04": {"followable": true, "why": "Bitcoin stays the referent and the clip self-explains ('everything... eventually bleeds to Bitcoin'), though 'also' nods to an unstated earlier example."}}}
